summary: Init reaps an orphan on its SIGCHLD, the log init's services write to is bounded within a boot, and a log a boot left full is removed at the next; the scenario is machine/servicelog_scenario.c and the log's bound is in utils/init.c

cases.behavior: on an ext2 root with init-shell as its init, init reaps each of ten orphans within two hundredths of a second of its end, by /proc/uptime, in at least eight of the ten; a service log filled past its cap of 256 KiB is emptied within the boot to the one line init writes, once orphans have turned init's loop; filled again and left by a power-off, it is removed at the next boot

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the copy of the root to its root shell
make ten orphans, each a sleep of a second, and note the uptime when each is first seen a zombie and when it is gone
fill the log past its cap, make orphans until init empties it, fill it again and power off
boot the same copy again to its root shell
read the log's size and its lines saying it was emptied, and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: of ten orphans, at least eight are gone within two hundredths of a second of the reading each was first seen a zombie in, as /proc/uptime counts them
the first boot fills the log past its cap
init empties the log within the boot, leaving less than 4 KiB and one line saying that it reached its limit
the log is filled past its cap again
the first boot ends by QEMU's SHUTDOWN event
the kernel says that it unmounted the root at the power-off
at the second boot the log has less than 4 KiB and no line saying that it was emptied, since init removed the full one

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case boots a root whose init is init-shell, fills its service log and powers the machine off
